brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut — they keep 7.4% profit vs 5.0% typical, so there's room; and line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source since we're only 0.01% of their business.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price cut on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Benchmark to the market typical band of ₹0.85–0.95/pc for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap, and push toward the headroom at ₹0.65–0.80 at our volume
priceAsk.basis: They keep 7.4% profit on every sale, well above the 5.0% that similar firms keep — that gap shows there's room in the price they charge us. The open-market ask for caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95, and the verdict says there's modest headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (cutting our 30 Days After Receipt in half) in exchange for a price cut of around 3–4%
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹1.64 L of our cash, but it's worth about 3.5% annually to them (half their 7.02% borrowing rate) — so trade that speed for a matching price cut

brief.financialLeverage: PGP Glass is healthy — rated CARE A+ / Stable, makes ₹3373.51 Cr in sales, and keeps 7.4% profit (vs 5.0% typical) — so they can afford to move on price. Their cash is stuck for 78 days, a bit longer than similar firms at 71d, meaning cash is slightly tight for them. But we're tiny — just 0.01% of their sales at ₹39.99 L — so on our own we have almost no pull. The play: bundle more volume or a multi-year commit, and quietly line up Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr, the country's largest rigid-plastic converter) or Mold-Tek (₹946.50 Cr, listed, strong) as a credible second source to show we have options.
